pairs: You shall cross over the Jordan today,
ut possideas nationes maximas et fortiores te,
very great and stronger than yourself,
cities vast and walled even to the sky,
whom you yourselves have seen and heard,
quibus nullus potest ex adverso resistere.
against whom no one is able to stand.
Scies ergo hodie quod Dominus Deus tuus ipse transibit ante te,
Therefore, you shall know today that the Lord your God himself will pass over before you,
like a devouring and consuming fire,
qui conterat eos, et deleat atque disperdat ante faciem tuam velociter,
to crush and to wipe away and to utterly ruin them before your face, quickly,
just as he has spoken to you.
You should not say in your heart,
cum deleverit eos Dominus Deus tuus in conspectu tuo:
when the Lord your God will have destroyed them in your sight:
Propter justitiam meam introduxit me Dominus ut terram hanc possiderem,
‘It is because of my justice that the Lord led me in, so that I might possess this land,
cum propter impietates suas istæ deletæ sint nationes.
while these nations have been destroyed because of their impiety.’
For it is not because of your justices
or the uprightness of your heart that you will enter,
so that you may possess their lands.
it is because they have acted wickedly that they are destroyed upon your arrival,
et ut compleret verbum suum Dominus,
and so that the Lord may accomplish his word,
quod sub juramento pollicitus est patribus tuis,
which he promised under oath to your fathers,
Scito ergo quod non propter justitias tuas Dominus Deus tuus dederit tibi terram hanc optimam in possessionem,
Therefore, know that the Lord your God will not give you this excellent land as a possession due to your justices,
for you are a very stiff-necked people.
quomodo ad iracundiam provocaveris Dominum Deum tuum in solitudine.
how you provoked the Lord your God to anger in the wilderness.
You have always contended against the Lord,
quo egressus es ex Ægypto usque ad locum istum,
from the day that you went forth from Egypt,
Nam et in Horeb provocasti eum,
For at Horeb also, you provoked him, and,
becoming angry, he was willing to destroy you,
when I ascended onto the mountain,
so that I might receive the tablets of stone,
tabulas pacti quod pepigit vobiscum Dominus:
the tablets of the covenant which the Lord formed with you.
et perseveravi in monte quadraginta diebus ac noctibus,
And I persevered on the mountain for forty days and nights,
Deditque mihi Dominus duas tabulas lapideas scriptas digito Dei, et continentes omnia verba quæ vobis locutus est in monte de medio ignis,
And the Lord gave me two tablets of stone, written with the finger of God and containing all the words that he spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of fire,
while the people, being stirred up, were assembled together.
And when forty days, and as many nights,
et totidem noctes, dedit mihi Dominus duas tabulas lapideas,
had passed, the Lord gave me the two tablets of stone,
whom you led away from Egypt,
deseruerunt velociter viam, quam demonstrasti eis,
have quickly abandoned the way that you have shown to them,
and they have made a molten idol for themselves.’
And again, the Lord said to me:
Cerno quod populus iste duræ cervicis sit:
‘I discern that this people is stiff-necked.
et deleam nomen ejus de sub cælo,
so that I may crush them,
and abolish their name from under heaven,
and appoint you over a nation,
which will be greater and stronger than this one.’
And as I was descending from the burning mountain,
et duas tabulas fœderis utraque tenerem manu,
and I held the two tablets of the covenant with both hands,
vidissemque vos peccasse Domino Deo vestro,
and I had seen that you had sinned against the Lord your God,
and had made a molten calf for yourselves,
and had quickly abandoned his way,
which he had revealed to you,
I threw down the tablets from my hands,
and I broke them in your sight.
Et procidi ante Dominum sicut prius,
And I fell prostrate before the Lord,
quadraginta diebus et noctibus panem non comedens,
just as before, for forty days and nights, not eating bread,
propter omnia peccata vestra quæ gessistis contra Dominum,
because of all your sins, which you had committed against the Lord,
and because you provoked him to anger.
timui enim indignationem et iram illius,
For I feared his indignation and wrath,
which had been stirred up against you,
so that he was willing to destroy you.
Et exaudivit me Dominus etiam hac vice.
And the Lord heeded me at this time also.
Likewise, he became vehemently angry against Aaron,
voluit eum conterere, et pro illo similiter deprecatus sum.
and he was willing to destroy him, and I prayed for him similarly.
But as for your sin which you committed, that is,
and reducing it entirely to dust,
projeci in torrentem, qui de monte descendit.
I threw it into the torrent that descends from the mountain.
et in Sepulchris concupiscentiæ provocastis Dominum:
and at the Graves of Lust, you provoked the Lord.
et quando misit vos de Cadesbarne,
And when he sent you from Kadesh-barnea,
which I have given to you,’
et contempsistis imperium Domini Dei vestri,
you spurned the command of the Lord your God,
and you did not believe him,
nor were you willing to listen to his voice.
sed semper fuistis rebelles a die qua nosse vos cœpi.
Instead, you were ever rebellious, from the day when I first began to know you.
Et jacui coram Domino quadraginta diebus ac noctibus,
And so, I lay prostrate before the Lord for forty days and nights,
as I humbly begged him, lest he destroy you,
ne deleret vos ut fuerat comminatus:
just as he had threatened to do.
do not destroy your people and your inheritance,
whom you have redeemed in your greatness,
quos eduxisti de Ægypto in manu forti.
whom you have led away from Egypt with a strong hand.
Do not look upon the stubbornness of this people,
nor upon their wickedness and sinfulness.
Otherwise, perhaps the inhabitants of the land,
out of which you have led us,
Non poterat Dominus introducere eos in terram,
may say: “The Lord was not able to lead them into the land,
so that he might put them to death in the wilderness.”
qui sunt populus tuus et hæreditas tua,
These are your people and your inheritance,
quos eduxisti in fortitudine tua magna,
whom you have led out by your great strength,
